xray.level: Standard X-ray (level 3), run on the standard catalogue and reviewed by a person

labels.read: Stated in a document you sent. We quote it and say where.
labels.computed: Arithmetic on your data. Re-run it with tools/recompute.py; every figure is checked.
labels.inferred: Our reading of two or more documents together. Check it before acting on it.

answers.question: Why is profit down when revenue is up?
answers.answer: Because cleaning costs rose and cleaning prices did not. Revenue is up 3.9% a month, and net profit has halved. Almost all of the fall is cleaning labour: two National Living Wage rises have passed since the last price change in January 2025. A 4.8% rise on cleaning prices would restore last year's cleaning margin.

answers.question: How exposed are we to Calder Retail Group?
answers.answer: More than the plan allows, and at a sensitive moment. Calder is 31% of revenue against a target of no customer above 20%, and the six new stores would take it to 34%. Its contract appears to reach its notice date on 30 September, two weeks before the board meets, and its complaints nearly tripled after the Manchester supervisor left.

answers.question: What should the board be looking at that it is not?
answers.answer: Six things: the notice dates on 30 September; complaints, which appear in no minutes; the price review, deferred twice; one action carried forward at three meetings; four jobs resting on one person each; and staff using personal ChatGPT accounts with customer information and no rule to cover it.

findings.label: computed
findings.title: Revenue is up 3.9% a month. Net profit has halved.
findings.detail: Last year (April 2025 to March 2026) the business averaged £343,350 of revenue and £15,717 of net profit a month, a net margin of 4.6%. From April to August 2026 it averaged £356,600 and £7,780, a net margin of 2.2%. The step is in April 2026, and it has not recovered in any month since.

evidence.text: Net by month is in xray/evidence/net-by-month.csv: 4.2% to 5.5% every month to March 2026; 1.9% to 2.4% every month from April.

findings.so_what: At 2.2%, one bad month or one lost contract puts the business at break-even. The plan's target is 8%.
findings.action: Take the monthly net margin to every board meeting, by service line, as the plan already says to do.

findings.label: computed
findings.title: The fall is almost all cleaning labour.
findings.detail: Cleaning's gross margin fell from 19.8% to 16.0%, because direct labour went from 74.4% to 78.2% of cleaning revenue. Reactive maintenance held at 34.0% and planned maintenance at 27.0%. Overheads rose by £2,500 a month. The lower cleaning margin cost about £41,200 in the five months to August, around £99,000 over a year.

evidence.text: Margin by line and period is in xray/evidence/margin-by-line.csv.

findings.so_what: The problem is narrow and known: a price that has not kept up with a cost. It is not the maintenance side, and it is not overheads.
findings.action: Price review on cleaning, starting with the contracts that have no indexation clause (F03).

findings.label: computed
findings.title: Prices have not moved since January 2025. Wages have moved twice.
findings.detail: The price list is dated 1 January 2025. Since then the National Living Wage rose 6.7% in April 2025 and 4.1% in April 2026. The board noted the second rise in January and deferred the price review in April; it is not on the July agenda. Three quarters of revenue sits in contracts with no indexation clause, so those prices only move if somebody asks. A 4.8% rise on cleaning would restore last year's cleaning margin.

evidence.text: Effective 1 January 2025.
Price review to be considered after the increase is confirmed.
Carried forward; Helen wants to avoid unsettling Calder before its six new stores are confirmed.
Only Pennine Housing Trust, Wharfe Valley Schools Trust and Kirkgate Medical Partnership have indexation: 25.0% of revenue.
National Living Wage: £11.44 to £12.21 in April 2025, £12.21 to £12.71 in April 2026.

findings.so_what: Every month without a review costs about £8,000 of margin on cleaning.
findings.action: Write the price review in October: a proposed rise per contract, the notice each contract needs, and which conversations to have first.

findings.title: Staff use personal ChatGPT accounts for customer work, and no rule covers it.
findings.detail: Nine staff use ChatGPT on their own accounts to write quotes, emails and method statements. The company does not pay for or manage those accounts. The handbook says customer information must only be stored in company systems, and that the company holds personal data about customers' staff and residents, but it was last reviewed in March 2021 and says nothing about AI tools. In personal accounts the company cannot see them, keep them or remove them when somebody leaves, and on consumer plans the account holder, not the company, chooses whether chats may be used for training.
findings.action: Keep the benefit and close the gap: a one-page rule for AI use, company accounts on business terms, and a list of what never goes into a prompt. RiskMandate.ai publishes a free twenty-minute exercise for writing down what an AI tool can reach and what you meant to allow.

# Northgate Facilities Ltd

*Copied from the company's website, "About us" page, August 2026. Northgate Facilities is an invented company.*

Northgate Facilities keeps buildings across Yorkshire and the North West clean, safe and working. Founded in Leeds in 2009, we now look after more than 200 sites for retailers, housing providers, schools, clinics, offices and hotels.

**What we do**

- **Contract cleaning**: daily, weekly and periodic cleaning, with our own trained teams.
- **Reactive maintenance**: a 24/7 helpdesk and engineers who attend within four hours for emergencies.
- **Planned maintenance**: statutory compliance and planned preventative maintenance (PPM) schedules, from fire doors to heating and ventilation.

**Why customers choose us**

- One partner for cleaning and maintenance.
- A named supervisor for every site.
- Real-time job reporting through our mobile platform.
- Quality audits on every site, every month.

**Our people.** Around 140 people, from our Leeds head office and our Manchester team.

*Northgate Facilities Ltd, invented. Handbook last reviewed March 2021.*

## 7. IT and acceptable use

7.1 Company devices and accounts are for company business. Reasonable personal use is allowed.
7.2 Do not install software on company devices without approval from the Office Manager.
7.3 Customer information must only be stored in company systems (Microsoft 365, FieldDesk, ServiceBook).
7.4 Passwords must not be shared, except through the office password manager.

## 8. Data protection

8.1 We hold personal data about staff and about customers' staff and residents, for example names, phone numbers and access arrangements.
8.2 Do not send personal data to anyone outside the company without approval.
8.3 Report any loss of data to the Office Manager the same day.

## 9. Expenses

9.1 Claims must be submitted within 30 days with receipts.
9.2 Subscriptions and software must be approved in advance by the Finance Manager.

# Northgate 2028: our plan for the next three years

*Presented to the management board by Helen Marsh, 22 January 2026. Northgate Facilities Ltd is invented.*

## Where we are

We are a strong cleaning business with a growing maintenance arm. Cleaning pays the bills, but it is low-margin and labour-heavy, and our customers increasingly want one partner for everything.

## Where we want to be by March 2028

1. **Planned maintenance at 40% of revenue**, up from under a fifth today. Planned maintenance is recurring, higher-margin and harder to switch away from.
2. **No customer above 20% of revenue.**
3. **Net margin of 8%.**
4. **A second office in Manchester**, with its own supervisor team.

## How we will get there

- Hire a planned maintenance sales lead in 2026.
- Offer every cleaning customer a free compliance review, to open planned maintenance conversations.
- Only take new cleaning contracts at a margin of 22% or more.
- Invest in one job management system for the whole business.

## What we will measure

Revenue mix by service line, monthly. Customer concentration, quarterly. Net margin, monthly.

claude.PROJECT-INSTRUCTIONS.md:
# Project instructions: Northgate X-ray

*Paste everything below the line into the instructions of a new Claude Project (or a ChatGPT Project). Then upload the files listed in `UPLOAD-THESE.md`.*

---

You are helping the management team of Northgate Facilities Ltd, a cleaning and building maintenance company in Leeds and Manchester, to understand and act on an X-ray of their business.

The project knowledge contains two kinds of files:

1. **The company's own documents**, from the `inbox/` folder: management accounts, customers, complaints, the sales pipeline, the price list, the org chart, board minutes, the three-year plan, supplier contracts, the software inventory and a handbook extract. `intake.md` says what they wanted to know and what they chose not to send.
2. **The X-ray**, from the `xray/` folder: `X-RAY.md` with 14 findings (F01 to F14), `findings.json`, the board pack, the open questions, the ninety-day plan, and the derived tables in `evidence/`.

How to answer:

- **Cite the file** for every fact, as the X-ray does: the file name, and the row, line or section.
- **Keep the three labels apart.** Say whether something is *read* (stated in a document), *computed* (arithmetic on the data, and show the arithmetic) or *inferred* (a reading of several documents together, to be checked).
- **When the documents do not say, say so.** Do not fill a gap with a guess. Add it to a list of questions for the team.
- **Refer to findings by their number** (F05) when a question touches one, and say whether the new question changes it.
- **Do not overrule the X-ray silently.** If you think a finding is wrong, say which one, why, and what evidence would settle it.
- **Be brief and direct.** The readers are the Managing Director, the Chair, the Operations Director and the Finance Manager.

When the team adds a new document to the vault, it is their newest evidence; say which findings it changes.

# Questions to start with

**On the findings**

1. Walk me through F02: which months, which lines, and what would have to be true for the fall to be something other than labour?
2. Draft the price review for October. One row per cleaning customer: current indexation, notice needed, a proposed rise, and who should call them.
3. What would F05 look like if Calder gave notice on 30 September? Show the effect on monthly net profit.
4. Is there any evidence in the documents that the Manchester complaints started before the supervisor left?

**On the board**

5. Turn the board pack into a fifteen-minute talk for the Chair, with the three decisions we need.
6. Write the open-actions list for the 15 October meeting from all three sets of minutes, with the age of each action.

**On things the X-ray did not cover**

7. Which of the questions in `questions-for-you.md` could the documents we already have answer, at least partly?
8. What would you need to see to say anything about cash?

**On what to do next**

9. Draft a one-page AI use rule for a company this size, using the handbook's existing sections as the style.
10. Write the brief for a Manchester area supervisor, using the complaints log to say what the first ninety days must fix.
11. Which three suppliers should we renegotiate first, and why?
12. What should the Re-X-ray in December check, to show whether any of this worked?

# Setting up Claude to keep asking questions

Ten minutes, once.

1. **Create a Claude Project.** In Claude, open *Projects* and create one called "Northgate X-ray". Projects are available on every Claude plan, including free accounts, which can have up to five. Sharing a project with colleagues needs a Team or Enterprise plan; otherwise each person sets up their own.
2. **Paste the instructions.** Copy the text below the line in `PROJECT-INSTRUCTIONS.md` into the project's instructions.
3. **Upload the files.** Add these to the project's knowledge:
   - every file in `inbox/`
   - `xray/X-RAY.md`, `xray/findings.json`, `xray/board-pack.md`, `xray/questions-for-you.md`, `xray/next-90-days.md`
   - every file in `xray/evidence/`
4. **Ask your first question.** `TRY-ASKING.md` has twelve to start with.

**In ChatGPT** the same steps work with a ChatGPT Project: paste the instructions into the project's instructions and upload the same files.

**If you use Claude Code or another agent that runs `sgit`,** skip the upload: clone the vault, and the agent reads the files where they are, including anything added since.

**Which account.** Use a company account on business terms, not a personal one. By default Anthropic does not use inputs or outputs from its commercial products, such as Claude for Work (Team and Enterprise) and the API, to train models. On consumer plans the account holder chooses. Check the current terms on the day you set this up.

**When the documents change,** upload the new versions and remove the old ones, or clone the vault again.

plan.title: Company X-Ray: a company's own documents, read together
plan.one_line: A company drops its own documents into an encrypted vault. Agents run a catalogue of analyses across them, a person reviews the result, and within five working days the company gets back its questions answered, a one-page board pack, findings that each name the document and row they came from, and a Claude setup to keep asking. No connectors, no integrations, no access to anything.

problem.name: The documents exist. Nobody reads them together.
problem.text: Management accounts, a customer list, a complaints log, board minutes, the plan, the supplier list: each has an owner, and nobody sets one against another.

problem.name: The owner has a feeling, not a picture
problem.text: "Busier than ever and making less money." The reason is usually in the documents, a few rows apart in files that never meet.

problem.name: A chat window is not enough
problem.text: Anyone can paste a spreadsheet into an assistant. What they do not get is the right questions, arithmetic that re-runs, every claim tied to its evidence, and a person who checked it.

problem.name: Consultants are slow and dear
problem.text: A reading of the business by an adviser takes weeks and costs thousands. Most small companies never commission one.

problem.name: Integrations stall the sale
problem.text: Connecting to a company's accounts, mail and drive means security reviews and access contracts. Dropping files into a vault means the customer decides what is seen, and the sale closes the same day.

formula.name: An agent platform
formula.text: Claude or ChatGPT, with the operator's catalogue of analyses and prompts.

formula.name: A vault
formula.text: Encrypted on the device, one per customer: the documents in, the X-ray out, and the history of both.

formula.name: Your documents
formula.text: What you choose to send, and nothing more. No connectors, no logins.

formula.name: An X-ray, and a Claude setup
formula.text: Your questions answered, a board pack, evidence for every finding, and a project to keep asking in.

steps.name: Buy, and receive a key
steps.text: A standing payment link per level. The vault key arrives separately from the instructions, never on a page.

steps.name: Drop documents in
steps.text: Into the vault's inbox, with an intake form: why now, three questions, what was sent and what was left out.

steps.name: Agents run the catalogue
steps.text: Twelve analyses. Arithmetic written as a script first, then findings, each labelled and tied to its evidence.

steps.name: A person reviews
steps.text: Runs the script until every figure matches, reads every inferred finding against its evidence, and commits a review note.

steps.name: Delivered to the vault
steps.text: Board pack, X-ray, questions, ninety days. Done is a commit in the customer's history.

steps.name: Keep asking
steps.text: Project instructions and files for a Claude Project, or a ChatGPT Project. The conversation continues with the same evidence and the same rules.
